court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court No.1, Pune at Pune (M.J. Petition No.691 of 2005)
case_name: Madhu Sangmeshwar Dhyade vs Sangmeshwar Sharanappa Dhyade
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1998 and had a son born in 2004. The respondent-husband filed for divorce on the ground of cruelty under section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court allowed the petition and dissolved the marriage.

legal_principles.principle: A party's version of events is not conclusive evidence, and the court must consider all relevant facts.
legal_principles.held: Once this Petition was served upon the Appellant - wife, she appeared in the matter and controverted all the allegations in her written statement (Exh.13).

legal_principles.principle: A party's denial of allegations does not necessarily mean those allegations are false.
legal_principles.held: The Appellant - wife denied almost all the allegations leveled against her in the Petition. She denied that she was cruel to the Respondent during the entire period of co-habitation .

outcome.final_order: The marital ties between the parties were dissolved by a decree of divorce as contemplated under section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
